title: A Microcontroller Operated Device for the Generation of Liquid Extracts from Conventional Cigarette Smoke and Electronic Cigarette Aerosol
protocol: Secure a 100 mL Buchner flask to a steel ring stand.
Fill the Buchner flask with 50 g of calcium chloride.
Seal the flask with a rubber through-hole stopper.
Wrap the stopper junction with paraffin film.
Run a pipette through the hole in the stopper.
Connect the pipette extending from the stopper to a t-intersection hose connector using vinyl tubing.
Connect the two impingers to each other using vinyl tubing.
Connect the output of the second impinger to the t-intersection hose connector using vinyl tubing.
Connect the input port of the first impinger as an inhalation port using vinyl tubing.
Connect the side arm of the Buchner flask to the input port of an airflow regulator using vinyl tubing.
Connect the exit port of the airflow regulator to a vacuum pump using vinyl tubing.
Assemble the circuit according to the schematic in Figure 2A.
Upload the PBASIC program SVL.bs1 to the BS1 microcontroller by means of a serial adaptor and the manufacturer's software.
Place the 510 threaded base in a ring stand clamp.
Connect the solenoid valve to the free end of the t-intersection hose connector using vinyl tubing.
Store all unopened conventional and electronic cigarette samples in the dark in airtight plastic bags at room temperature.
Once opened, store samples in airtight plastic bags at 4 ºC with a paper towel to absorb excess moisture.
Pre-equilibrate all samples in a room temperature humidor at ~60% humidity for at least 30 minutes prior to use.
Determine the mass of each e-cigarette cartomizer/tank pre-vaping using an analytical balance.
Fill the reservoir of the primary impinger with 4.3 mL of endothelial cell culture medium.
Fill the reservoir with 5 mL of acetone.
Apply a piece of clear tape around the filter and put an easily visible mark where the cigarette paper joins the filter.
Ensure the battery is well charged and the cartomizer is tightly screwed to the battery for e-cigarettes.
Load an appropriate volume of electronic cigarette liquid in the tank and screw the tank onto the 510 threaded base.
Insert the tip of the conventional or electronic cigarette into the inhalation port.
Secure the tip with a hose clamp.
Turn on the vacuum pump.
Adjust the flow meter to pull 1.65 L/minute for a 55 mL puff over 2 seconds.
Light the cigarette on the first puff for conventional cigarettes.
Run until projected desired concentration is achieved.
Determine the mass of each e-cigarette cartomizer/tank after vaporization using an analytical balance.
Compare this measurement to the initial measurement to determine the total mass consumed.
Calculate the concentration of the consumed mass/volume of solvent.
Normalize between products using the molar concentration of consumed nicotine.
Return the electronic cigarette to the device and consume further if insufficient mass was consumed.
Proceed if a sufficient or excess mass was consumed.
Filter extracts through a 0.22 µm PES syringe filter for cell culture use.
Use the extracts immediately or store at -80°C.
Rinse the tubing and reservoirs of the device with 70% ethanol after each extraction.
Rinse the tubing and reservoirs with deionized water to prevent carry over between samples.
Briefly run the empty device to assist drying of the lines.
Perform extract into 4.3 mL of endothelial cell growth medium for Neutral Red Uptake Cell Viability Assay.
Seed human umbilical vein endothelial cells into 96 well plates at a density of 1 x 10^4 cells/well in 100 μL of endothelial cell growth medium.

Replace old endothelial cell culture medium with either 100 μL of fresh endothelial cell culture medium as control or 75 μL of endothelial cell growth medium mixed with 25 μL of a 2 mM nicotine extract for treatment at a final concentration of 500 µM.
Seal the wells airtight using foil to prevent volatilization of components.
Incubate the plate 18–24 h at 37 °C and 5% CO2.
Create a 100x neutral red stock solution by dissolving 33 mg of neutral red dye into 10 mL of buffered salt solution.
Dilute 100x stock solution 1:100 in cell culture medium to create 1x neutral red staining solution shortly before use.
Incubate the neutral red staining solution at 37 °C for at least 30 min prior to use and use immediately.
Remove extract and add 100 µL of neutral red staining solution per well.
Incubate the plate at 2–4 h at 37 °C and 5% CO₂.
Remove neutral red staining solution and wash 3x by submersion in PBS.
Apply neutral red de-stain solution (50% deionized water, 49% ethanol, 1% acetic acid).
Incubate for at least 10 min at room temperature with shaking.
Read absorbance at 540 nm.
